entries.claim: Expected squared prediction error decomposes into squared bias, variance and irreducible noise, giving the bias-variance tradeoff over model complexity
entries.locator: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, Chapter 7

entries.claim: L2 (ridge) regularization corresponds to a Gaussian prior on the weights and L1 (lasso) to a Laplace prior, linking penalised regression to Bayesian posteriors
entries.locator: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning, ridge and lasso

entries.claim: K-fold cross-validation partitions the data into K folds and uses each in turn as validation data, so every observation is validated exactly once
entries.notes: Supports figure 2 and the CV section

entries.claim: Dropout at test time can be interpreted as approximate Bayesian model averaging
entries.notes: Supports the 'black magic has statistical roots' callout

entries.claim: Batch Normalization was motivated in part by reducing internal covariate shift
entries.notes: Claim stated as the authors' motivation

entries.claim: XGBoost adds an explicit regularisation term for the number of leaves and the L2 norm of leaf weights to the boosting objective
The bias-variance demo functions, the R-squared values of 0.998 and 0.87, and the error curves are constructed teaching illustrations
entries.notes: Not results from any real modelling project

entries.claim: The bias-variance U-curve and the K-fold partition figures are teaching diagrams prepared for this lesson
